slides.title: Q1 review: East leads, the rest holds
slides.subtitle: Regional performance, January – March 2026

say: This quarter one region pulled clearly ahead and the other three held steady.
I will show you what East did differently and ask you to fund the same playbook everywhere.

slides.title: East grew faster than any region
slides.caption: East revenue vs Q4, constant currency

say: East grew 8 % on the previous quarter, faster than any other region, according to the April finance dashboard.
That is in constant currency with one-offs taken out, so it is real growth, not an exchange-rate effect.

points: Partner-led sales and weekly pipeline reviews

slides.title: East leads Q1, up 8 %
slides.caption: North's dip is seasonal and repeats every Q1.

say: Here is the same quarter region by region: East is up 8 %, South 3 %, West is flat and North is down 1.5 %.
North's dip is seasonal and repeats every first quarter.
The figures are from the April finance dashboard.

slides.title: Margins rose while costs held

say: Margins rose 1.5 points this quarter while operating costs stayed flat, according to the April finance dashboard.
That is why I am asking for the partner budget now: growth is not costing us margin.

slides.decision: Fund the partner programme in every region: 410 k this year

slides.title: East's playbook differs in two ways

say: When we interviewed the regional leads in March, East's approach stood out in two ways.
East sells through partners where the others sell direct, and it reviews its pipeline every week instead of every month.

slides.title: Rolling it out takes four steps

say: Rolling the playbook out takes four steps, and sales operations owns all of them.
I will walk through them in order; the slide shows what each one hands over to the next.

slides.title: Every region runs the playbook by October

say: If we start now, every region runs the playbook by October.
The dates hold only if partner contracts are signed by mid-May, so that is the first thing I will track.
assumptions: Dates assume partner contracts by mid-May

slides.title: Partners give the most for the least effort

say: Of everything East tried, partners gave the most result for the least effort.
That ranking comes from the scoring we did together in the March workshop.
assumptions: Effort and value scores are the workshop's judgement, not measured data

slides.title: What the East team says
slides.quote: The weekly review is where the deals actually move.

say: I will let the East team speak for themselves here.
Read the quote out, then pause before moving on - it is the best summary of why the playbook works.

slides.title: East's growth came from the city centre
slides.caption: Illustration.

say: Most of East's growth came from the city centre.
The picture is an illustration, not a photo of our stores.

slides.title: Only East beat its target

say: Only East beat its target this quarter, according to the 2026 plan and the April finance dashboard.
East finished 8 % over its target; the other three regions ended within 3 % of theirs.

slides.title: East pulled ahead every month of the quarter

say: East did not win on one good month: its lead over the other regions widened in every month of the quarter.
The monthly figures are from the April finance dashboard.

slides.title: Two risks could stall the rollout

risks.mitigation: Start with the two partners East already works with; add others from June.
Each region's owner reports at the monthly leadership meeting.

say: Two risks could stall the rollout, and partner pace is the one that matters most.
If partners sign slowly, every date on the timeline moves, so that is where mitigation effort goes first.
assumptions: Likelihood and impact ratings are the team's assessment, not data

slides.title: The rollout costs 410 k this year
slides.note: Partner fees are paid only on closed deals.

say: The rollout costs 410 thousand this year in total, according to the April budget draft.
Most of that is paid only when partners deliver results, so the money at risk up front is small.

Can you join the kick-off on 12 May? It takes two hours.

say: Before I show the answer, which region do you think beat its target?
Take a few answers from the room, then reveal it.

slides.title: Three decisions for today

say: That leaves three decisions for today.
The budget detail behind them is in the appendix if anyone wants to go through it.

slides.title: We will call the rollout a success at these targets
slides.rule: Stop rule: if partner deals stay under 20 % by July, we pause and review.

say: We will call the rollout a success if we hit three targets, each with an owner and a date.
There is also one stop rule, so we know in advance when to pull back.
pitfalls: The targets are examples; set them with Finance before presenting them as agreed

The one decision I need from you today is the partner budget.
